text:
Taylor: Heads-up  I found inconsistent examples for the /keys/{id}/verify response. Some examples show `fingerprint` as lowercase hex (e.g. "a1b2c3"), others show base64 (e.g. "obLD"). Backend canonical format is base64; hex was left over from a previous doc conversion.

Morgan: Good catch. Which files have the hex examples?

Taylor: I found hex in the OpenAPI examples for /keys/{id}/verify and in a couple of SDK snippets (Go and Ruby). The real API returns base64 strings. This has caused a couple of integration errors in support tickets where customers tried to compare hex to base64.

Diego: We should standardize to base64 everywhere, and add a tiny conversion snippet for folks who still store hex. Also add a short migration note: "fingerprint is base64-encoded by the service; convert legacy hex values using helper provided below."

Morgan: Agreed. Plan: 1) Update OpenAPI example values to base64. 2) Fix curl/python/js/go snippets to expect base64. 3) Add a small code snippet (py/go) showing hex<->base64 conversion. 4) Add docs-e2e lint that fails if any `fingerprint` example matches `^[0-9a-fA-F]+$` (i.e., pure hex).

Taylor: I'll open the draft PR with the OpenAPI changes and example updates. Diego, can you prepare the conversion snippets for inclusion and a short blurb in the migration guide?

Diego: On it. Example snippets below:

Python:
```python
import base64, binascii
# hex_to_base64
hex_val = 'a1b2c3d4'
base64_val = base64.b64encode(binascii.unhexlify(hex_val)).decode('ascii')
# base64_to_hex
hex_back = binascii.hexlify(base64.b64decode(base64_val)).decode('ascii')
```

Go:
```go
import (
  "encoding/base64"
  "encoding/hex"
)
// hex -> base64
h := "a1b2c3d4"
b, _ := hex.DecodeString(h)
b64 := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(b)
// base64 -> hex
b2, _ := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(b64)
h2 := hex.EncodeToString(b2)
```

Morgan: Nice and concise. For the SDK changes: do not change serialized types (they remain string)  only examples and snippets. We'll avoid a breaking-change note.

Taylor: docs-bot, please create an issue and a draft PR linking the OpenAPI and snippets edits and include the lint rule.

docs-bot: Created issue #2299 and draft PR #3251: https://git.redwood/g/infra/docs/pulls/3251 (OpenAPI example updates, SDK snippet fixes, conversion snippets, docs-e2e lint for fingerprint format).

Diego: I'll push conversion snippets and a one-line migration paragraph to the PR branch this afternoon. ETA: 3 hours.

Morgan: I'll review PR after Diego pushes. Also quick test idea: add a docs smoke test that parses the generated HTML and asserts fingerprint examples decode as valid base64 (regex `^[A-Za-z0-9+/]+=*$`).

Taylor: Love it. Thanks all :thumbsup: Once merged I'll add a note in the next docs release notes and close related support tickets that cited this confusion.
